utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Thursday, January 17, 2008, and I welcome Mrs. Dahl, the witness, Mr. Seselj, and everyone helping us around the courtroom. I will now give an oral decision. Oral decision on lifting the confidentiality of the transcript of January 15, 2008. Noting the verbal request of the accused of January 15th, 2008 in order to lift the confidentiality of the excerpts of the transcript on page 2306, line 5 to 21 for the French transcript, noting that this excerpt deals with the existence of a motion submitted by the accused on December 11, 2007, and filed by the registrar as document 359, confidential document, noting that the content of this document number 359 must continue to be confidential since the name of witnesses being -- having been granted protective measures are mentioned, but since this submission 359 may be made public, as well as what was said during the hearing and which is on the transcript on page 2306, line 5 to 21, for these reasons, according to Rule -- to Article 20 of the Statute and Rule 54 and 75 of the regulation grants the oral submission of the accused and makes public lines 5 to 21 of page 2306 of the French transcript dated January 15, 2008. Very well. Mrs. Dahl, you now have the floor to finish off your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something before that? Before the examination-in-chief starts, I have four brief requests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask the Trial Chamber to look at the possibility of the first 40 minutes of yesterday's hearing be made public. In my view, there is not a single reason why that part of the session should remain inaccessible to the public. Furthermore, during the course of the day, perhaps up until the first break, we should receive the text of the SMS messages that had been received. Before you rule on this, I'm not going to say what it is actually but we all understand what this is all about. Two more requests unrelated to that but they have to do with our work afterwards. The Prosecution requested to include Witness VS-046 [as interpreted] on its list of confidential witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 44, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had them on their list previously and they gave up on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. There must have been a mistake you said VS-044 and here on the transcript it says VS-046 so you were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we corrected it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 46, right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 44 [as interpreted], yes. In the meantime, the man established contact with my legal advisors and agreed to be a Defence counsel and after that Ms. Dahl looked for him, went to his home and asked that he be a Prosecution witness which he categorically refused. He made a statement before the court in Belgrade, before the police and sent her a letter to that effect. Fourthly, very importantly, it would be very important that I receive the text of the judgement in the case of the Vukovar troika before the next witness is heard who is going to speak about Vukovar. It's not indispensable for cross-examining this witness, but it's going to be very important for the next witness. So could you please intervene with the Registry to have this brought to an end as soon as possible. I haven't received a copy yet, and you will understand why that judgement is so very important for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have made these four submissions, and the Trial Chamber will look into that. Regarding the fourth request on the Vukovar judgement, I'm sure that you're talking about the judgement made by this Tribunal in the Mrkic case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously that's the one. This trial judgement was rendered in English. I think it's more than 300 pages long. I know of a previous judgement which I rendered and it was in French and it was 800 pages long and the translation service took about a year to translate those 800 pages. So if this trial judgement is to be translated into your judgement in your own -- in your own language and if -- since it's probably very long it will probably take some time, but I'm sure that a number of your associates speak and understand English, and they can probably identify in the judgement the excerpts that are of specific relevance to you. Then just tell us then what pages you want translated first. You know that in a trial judgement you have very general paragraphs but also paragraphs that are very relevant to you. So your associates just have to check and see what paragraphs are relevant to your case and then we will press the translation services to make sure that they translate these first and we get them quickly. This is a possibility that you should look into, because asking the translation service to translate these 300 pages in your own language is not going to be possible. It's just -- I know the answer, you know, without having to ask it. The legal officer will check where we stand in terms of this translation, and we'll try and find a solution. As to the three other items, the three other motions, we'll see Witness 44, the problem of the SMSs, and the question of the 41st pages. Very well. Mrs. Dahl, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj once more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you know that not a single one of my legal associates speaks the English or the French language. When we check the transcripts, and I already told you that we did that, with the transcripts in one session we engaged and paid a professional translator to do this for us. To pay a professional translator for a 300-page-long judgement is too expensive. We don't have that kind of money. My debt is already too big and the Registry has to translate this one way or the other into the Serbian language and their translation is the official one. Why should this be done twice if the Registry has to have this translated into Serbian one way or the other. This is just a question of priority in translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll take what you just said into account while we look into this. Mrs. Dahl, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We need to go into private session to address a matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Partial hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of January, 2008, at 2.45 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.07 a.m.,
